mechanism_inventory: precision/truncation loss in price calculation (sellAmount * price / Constants.Q96 and buyAmount * price / Constants.Q96 truncates toward zero, systematically under-compensating pool)

stale accounting snapshot / wrong value flow in buy() — maxQuoteAmount taken from pool but only quoteAmount (price-based) returned, leaving a residual difference unaccounted if price != 0 branch sends wrong amount back

value exceeds a logical/economic bound — fee parameter is caller-controlled (SettlementParams.fee), allowing sender to set arbitrarily large positive fee extracted via predyPool.take() or negative fee pulled from themselves, with no cap validation

external-call failure / DoS — ISettlement.swapExactIn / swapExactOut are external calls to a user-supplied contractAddress (whitelisted but still external); a malicious or buggy settlement contract could revert, locking execution

victim accounting direction — in buy() with price != 0 branch: predyPool.take(true, address(this), settlementParams.maxQuoteAmount) withdraws maxQuoteAmount from pool, but safeTransfer back to pool is maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmount (not maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni), so quoteAmount of quote tokens is NOT returned to pool — the difference (quoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni) when quoteAmount > quoteAmountToUni is sent to sender instead of being reconciled with pool
missing invariant enforcement — no check that quoteAmountFromUni >= some minimum (other than maxQuoteAmount used as minQuoteAmount in sell) actually enforces pool-accounting correctness

hook caller or hook-timing mismatch — settlement callback executes arbitrary external code (swapExactIn/swapExactOut) between pool.take() and pool repayment, creating a window where pool balances are transiently inconsistent and a reentrancy or callback could observe stale state

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: In buy() with price != 0 branch: predyPool.take(true, address(this), settlementParams.maxQuoteAmount) withdraws maxQuoteAmount quote tokens from the pool. The function then calls swapExactOut which returns quoteAmountToUni (actual quote spent). If quoteAmount (= buyAmount * price / Q96) > quoteAmountToUni, the difference is sent to sender (line: safeTransfer(sender, quoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni)). Then safeTransfer to predyPool is maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmount. The total returned to pool = maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmount. But the total taken was maxQuoteAmount and total spent on swap was quoteAmountToUni. The pool should receive back maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni. Instead it receives maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmount. If quoteAmount > quoteAmountToUni, pool is shortchanged by (quoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni) which went to sender. Net pool loss = quoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni when price-based quoteAmount exceeds actual swap cost.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Any party who controls settlementParams (filler/market maker) can manipulate price parameter to set quoteAmount > quoteAmountToUni, extracting the difference from the pool at pool/LP expense. This is permissionless in the sense that fillers can submit orders with crafted price values.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker (filler) crafts a buy order with high price parameter such that buyAmount * price / Q96 > actual market quoteAmountToUni. 2. execSettlement -> buy() is called. 3. predyPool.take(true, this, maxQuoteAmount) takes maxQuoteAmount from pool. 4. swapExactOut spends quoteAmountToUni (actual, less than quoteAmount). 5. Since quoteAmount > quoteAmountToUni: sender receives (quoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni) surplus. 6. Pool receives only maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmount instead of maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni. 7. Pool is net short (quoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni) in quote tokens.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: PredyPool / liquidity providers lose quote tokens equal to quoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: settlementParams.sender gains the surplus quote tokens.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Source-proven: the arithmetic in buy() returns maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmount to pool, not maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni. The two differ whenever quoteAmount != quoteAmountToUni. This directly extracts value from the pool to sender. High severity — direct fund loss from pool.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: In sell() with price != 0 branch: pool receives exactly quoteAmount (= sellAmount * price / Q96) regardless of actual swap output quoteAmountFromUni. If quoteAmountFromUni > quoteAmount, the surplus goes to sender. If quoteAmountFromUni < quoteAmount, sender must top up. The pool's accounting is based on the price-derived quoteAmount, not on actual market value. This is a design choice (filler bears slippage), but the asymmetry in buy() described above means the filler-accounting is inconsistently applied between sell and buy paths.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: In sell() path: if quoteAmountFromUni > quoteAmount (swap yields more than price implies), sender pockets the difference. No loss to pool here — pool gets quoteAmount. But combined with the buy() flaw, a filler can engineer scenarios where buy surplus is extracted from pool.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Pool in buy() path; sender in sell() path when market is worse than price (sender must top up).
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Sender in sell() when market is better than price.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Confirms the asymmetric accounting model and establishes that the sell-path correctly closes accounting (pool gets quoteAmount, surplus/deficit to sender), while buy-path does NOT correctly close (pool gets maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmount, not maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni), confirming the buy-path loss is a bug not a design.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: fee parameter manipulation — SettlementParams.fee is caller-supplied with no on-chain cap. A large positive fee causes predyPool.take(true, sender, fee) to extract fee amount of quote tokens from pool to sender. A large negative fee requires sender to transfer -fee tokens to pool before settlement. If fee can be set to an arbitrary large value, this is an uncapped extraction vector.
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: Lines 203-213: fee < 0 triggers safeTransferFrom(sender, predyPool, uint(-fee)); fee > 0 triggers predyPool.take(true, sender, uint(fee)). No cap check on fee magnitude in this library. Fee is part of SettlementParams passed by caller.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether fee is validated/capped upstream (in the calling market contract or order signature) before reaching execSettlement. The library itself has no cap. If the market contract does not enforce a fee cap or require fee to be signed by the user/order, an attacker can set fee to drain pool. Cannot determine from this file alone.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: PredyPool / LPs if fee is uncapped and positive fee can be set by attacker.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: precision loss in Q96 fixed-point division — sellAmount * price / Q96 and buyAmount * price / Q96 truncate toward zero. In sell(), truncation under-represents quoteAmount, meaning pool receives slightly less than fair value on each sell settlement. In buy(), truncation under-represents quoteAmount, which reduces the amount returned to sender when quoteAmount > quoteAmountToUni (less surplus to sender), but also reduces pool repayment (maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmount is larger when quoteAmount is smaller). Systematic truncation creates a per-trade accounting drift that may accumulate.
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: Lines 257, 281, 304, 328: uint256 quoteAmount = sellAmount * price / Constants.Q96 — Solidity integer division truncates.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether the truncation direction consistently favors or disfavors the pool, and whether the magnitude is dust-level or material at scale. Requires numeric analysis of realistic price/amount parameters.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Either pool or sender depending on which branch and direction.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: external-call reentrancy during swapExactIn/swapExactOut creating permanent false state
rejected_mechanisms.claimed_locus: ISettlement.swapExactIn / ISettlement.swapExactOut callback window between predyPool.take() and pool repayment
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: The settlement contractAddress is validated against a whitelist (_whiteListedSettlements) in the validate() function (lines 185-194). Only pre-approved settlement contracts can be called. While a window exists, the whitelist restricts which contracts can be invoked, substantially limiting reentrancy attack surface to trusted contracts.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: Settlement contracts are whitelisted; a malicious contract cannot be substituted. A compromised or buggy whitelisted contract is a different threat model requiring separate analysis. The reentrancy window exists but the attacker-controlled code path is blocked by whitelist.
rejected_mechanisms.who_loses: Pool if whitelisted contract were malicious.
rejected_mechanisms.leans_on_unproven_guard: Partially — the whitelist guard is in validate(), which must be called upstream of execSettlement. If any caller skips validate(), the guard is absent. However, the library structure separates validate() and execSettlement() intentionally, and this is an upstream caller responsibility, not a flaw in execSettlement itself.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Quote tokens extracted from PredyPool in buy() path when quoteAmount (price-derived) exceeds quoteAmountToUni (actual swap cost); the difference goes to settlementParams.sender rather than remaining in pool
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Attacker (filler) retains control of surplus and can repeat this on each buy settlement
impact_direction.victim_loses: PredyPool / liquidity providers lose quote tokens proportional to (quoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni) per buy settlement where price is set above market
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Pool solvency invariant: after buy settlement, pool should receive back maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmountToUni (net cost of swap); instead it receives maxQuoteAmount - quoteAmount, where quoteAmount != quoteAmountToUni
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: Loss comes from pool reserves, not attacker's own funds; magnitude scales with trade size and price deviation; not admin-gated (filler is the actor); not timing-dependent (structural arithmetic mismatch)
